audit.summary: The local obstruction depends on choices, and the fixed degree20 realization theorem has an exact counterexample. Further local quantifier, signature-characterization, dimension and root-hypothesis defects are proved.
limitations: Local residue exchanges are misclassified and epsilon is not choice independent — Counterevidence: The main quadratic input has an actual global hyperbolic realization diag(A,A^{-t}) plus−id onH². This is not a no-realization example, and not a counterexample to every Salem theorem.

Claim2 allows an impossible determinant in a single linear eigenspace — Counterevidence: H with identity realizes F. Proposition11.1 asks prescribed determinants only when both linear eigenspaces are present.

Signature-map characterization misses joint uniqueness and nonreal reciprocal blocks — Counterevidence: Joint multiplicity condition(d) resolves identity example; Salem-plus-cyclotomic spectra have no nonreal off-circle quartets.

Two auxiliary constructions have the wrong dimension — Counterevidence: Replacing exponent2 by4 restores degree and relevant endpoint-square conditions. Replacing complement by(1,21−degC) restores signature and congruence. Root reflections provide additional positive chamber evidence.
Theorem21.3 omits S(delta)=0 — Counterevidence: The introduction and notation already correctly restrict delta to a root of S.

Theorem24.1(a) fails for its specified degree20 characteristic polynomial — Counterevidence: Changing the cyclotomic factor can avoid the contradiction. The example does not disprove general degree20 Salem realizability or the broader result attributed to Takada.

proposition.claim:
Every admissible local datum gives the same epsilon pairing on C0(I).

F=f^2(X+1)^4, f=X^2−7X+1; signature(4,4), block signatures(2,2), D−=81 squareclass1; C0,C1 and delta=0 all hold.

Arbitrary units u+,u− with product(−1)^n can prescribe the extant component determinant.

F=(X−1)^2,n=1,n+=2,n−=0,F1=1,u+=1,u−=−1.

Conditions(a)–(e) characterize all semisimple real signature maps.

General real semisimple isometries, not only Salem-plus-cyclotomic spectra.

The displayed polynomials and complementary lattices have total rank22 and signature(3,19).

m=5 or8 in Case1; degC≡4mod8 in Proposition27.2 branch.

The stated realization holds for any complex delta with modulus1.

S=X4−X3−X2−X+1 is a degree4 Salem polynomial; delta is a primitive29th root.

Odd, square-free coprime endpoint values suffice for a realizable isometry with the fixed F and Salem signature.

S=X20+X19−sum_{j=3}^{17}X^j+X+1; S(1)=−11,S(−1)=1. Both meet the endpoint hypotheses.

repair.content:
Define exchanges from actual local residue images, including unramified nonsplit blocks reducing to±1, and reprove orbit/choice independence and global sufficiency.

Remove arbitrary determinant prescription for a sole linear eigenspace and choose total determinant consistently, using n where required; delete false parity inference.

State uniqueness after all multiplicity conditions; require balanced hyperbolic multiplicities for all non-self-reciprocal factors; define zero-polynomial convention.

Use Phi_m²(X−1)^4 and complementary signature(1,21−degC), then reconcile all later premises.

Add S(delta)=0.

Restrict the fixed-polynomial assertion or add discriminant/chamber compatibility; alternatively allow the cyclotomic factor to change.
